era.title: Near-Future Breakthroughs
era.subtitle: The first wave of civilization-changing discoveries
era.description: This era introduces breakthroughs in AI, robotics, medicine, climate technology, materials science, and early space automation.

seo.metaTitle: Era 1: Near-Future Breakthroughs | Future Civilization Roadmap
seo.metaDescription: Explore near-future breakthroughs in AI, robotics, cancer detection, climate materials, lunar robotics, and self-healing cities.

items.title: AI hospital triage becomes standard worldwide
items.description: Hospitals adopt AI triage systems that help classify urgency, detect early warning signs, route patients faster, and reduce pressure on emergency departments.
items.civilizationImpact: Healthcare becomes more proactive, faster, and more accessible, especially in overloaded public health systems.
signals: AI-assisted emergency intake tools become regulated medical software
Hospitals integrate triage models with electronic health records
Remote patient intake becomes common before physical arrival
implications: Shorter waiting times for urgent patients
New governance standards for medical AI accountability

items.title: Carbon-negative concrete enters mass production
items.description: New cement and concrete processes store more carbon than they emit, turning major construction projects into long-term carbon sinks.
items.civilizationImpact: Cities begin reducing their embodied carbon while continuing to expand infrastructure, housing, and public works.
signals: Carbon mineralization becomes cheaper at industrial scale
Building codes recognize verified carbon-storing materials
Large developers choose low-carbon materials by default
implications: New carbon accounting standards for buildings

signals: Multi-sensor wearables track blood, sleep, movement, and voice markers
AI models personalize disease-risk baselines
Insurance and health systems incentivize early detection
implications: More diseases detected at treatable stages
Greater demand for privacy-preserving health AI
Personal health dashboards become everyday infrastructure
